properties.caption: In the largest project on tap, Redwood Dev Co plans to develop nearly 2,200 apartments and it's starting this fall with two buildings: a 203-unit affordable project for tenants 55 and older, and a 255-unit one with market-, workforce- and affordable apartments.

In Northeast Miami-Dade County, Dezer Development is known for its long-planned Uptown Harbour mixed-use megaproject at the Intracoastal Mall. While Dezer's site plan still needs the green light from North Miami Beach officials, the developer proposed another project to the south: the nearly 600-unit mixed-use Dezerland Park West on the site of a truck parking lot in North Miami.

Uptown Harbour is planned for about 2,000 residential units, 375,000 square feet of retail, 200,000 square feet of offices and a 250-key hotel on the Intracoastal Mall that's on Sunny Isles Boulevard that connects North Miami Beach and Sunny Isles Beach.

Sales are underway at Blue Road and Ilia Development Group's 374-unit condo building, with asking prices ranging from $380,000 to more than $1 million for the condos, which will range from studios to three bedrooms. The 25-story building will include a rooftop pickleball courts.
In the latest neighborhood addition, Blue Road and Edgardo Defortuna’s Fortune International Group are about to wrap up development of the 16-story Nexo Residences with 254 condos.

South Florida developers are seizing on consolidating universities to redevelop former campuses. Case in point: PPG Development and its partners started building this year a 728-unit apartment complex on the former Nova Southeastern University site in North Miami Beach.

This is one of Continua Developments' pair of apartment projects on two of North Miami's main streets. In partnership with SP Developers, Continua is building this 12-story, 240-unit building on Northeast Sixth Avenue.
Continua Developments and Oldtown Capital Partners are expected to complete this 12-story, 195-unit building on northeast 125th Street.

Developer Daniel Abreu is developing the six-story, 80-unit building, marking one of the first Live Local Act projects to rise in South Florida. Although many developers have seized on the state law with project applications, few have scored construction loans or started building.

Father-daughter duo Ian Brice and Allie Eichner's Continuum Company plans a pair of 20-story glass condo buildings with 263 units, launching sales this year, with asking prices starting at $1.4 million. The developer completed the nearly $50 million bulk buyout of the aging condo building on the site now that dates back to the '80s.
Tate Capital wants to redevelop its North Miami headquarters with a 17-story, 348-unit apartment building, though it will first do a cost-revenue analysis.
Tate Capital, led by brothers James and Kenneth Tate, and developer Sergio Rok's long-planned 360-unit apartment building advanced this year with the extension of a city grant agreement.
In another nod to campus redevelopments in South Florida, Lore Development Group plans a 402-unit apartment building on a portion of the shuttered Johnson & Wales University campus.
